authorization: User: etymologise all Indo-Aryan SIL surveys jointly; do everything; surface tough/unclear cases for audit once done.

proposals.evidence: Previously reviewed comparative evidence: CDIAL gives Hindi *phal*, Gujarati/Marathi *phaḷ*, and eastern *phar*. The ph/ɸ and l/ḷ variants are direct comparanda; Bagheli’s retained l and -ua extension leave Hindi contact or local derivation open. Updated disposition under the user’s explicit cross-Indo-Aryan policy: link this supported etymon despite unresolved inheritance versus intra-Indo-Aryan borrowing. The reflex edge records etymological family affiliation provisionally; it does not establish uninterrupted inheritance or an immediate donor. Prior hold: Retained lateral in Bihari phal may indicate Hindi/Bengali contact; CDIAL distinguishes inherited phar from phal loans.

proposals.evidence: Previously reviewed comparative evidence: CDIAL 10875.2 *lakkuṭa lists Prakrit lakkuḍa, Hindi lakṛī “firewood”, Gujarati lākṛũ and Marathi lākuḍ “wood”. Retained k selects the strengthened branch; Maithili lakṛī is explicitly borrowed from Hindi and is held for an immediate-donor link. Updated disposition under the user’s explicit cross-Indo-Aryan policy: link this supported etymon despite unresolved inheritance versus intra-Indo-Aryan borrowing. The reflex edge records etymological family affiliation provisionally; it does not establish uninterrupted inheritance or an immediate donor. Prior hold: CDIAL 10875 explicitly labels eastern Maithili lakṛī a Hindi loan; local transmission needs evidence.

proposals.evidence: Previously reviewed comparative evidence: CDIAL 142 accha gives Punjabi acchā “good”, explicitly borrowed into standard Hindi, and Old Marwari āchyo/āchī. The route is decided locally: standard Hindi is linked to the existing Punjabi attestation; direct western āch- continuations are kept separate from unresolved regional contact forms. Updated disposition under the user’s explicit cross-Indo-Aryan policy: link this supported etymon despite unresolved inheritance versus intra-Indo-Aryan borrowing. The reflex edge records etymological family affiliation provisionally; it does not establish uninterrupted inheritance or an immediate donor. Prior hold: CDIAL 142 distinguishes inherited western āch- forms from Punjabi > Hindi acchā; the survey lect’s immediate borrowing route is not established.
